summary: Plan social studies, select sampling methods and assess evidence quality. Explore the five-day foundation course and choose your next step.
lede: Social research methods give research assistants, policy researchers and programme officers a structured way to investigate social questions and assess evidence. The course helps you turn a topic into a researchable question, choose and justify a suitable sample, and draft survey items; you also practise reviewing consent and confidentiality risks and interpreting descriptive findings with their limits.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who plan, support or review social studies and need a practical foundation for making research choices. It suits professionals working with survey, interview or observational evidence across public and community-facing services.
prerequisites: Bring a social research question or topic from your work to use in exercises. No coding is required.
topics: Data collection, survey design & mobile tools
